locator.text: Equation (4.14), p. 27, in the proof of Proposition 4.2

evidence: paper: (\partial_t + u_r^{(0)}\partial_r + u_z^{(0)}\partial_z)(q^{-h}H) \;=\; \frac{q^{-h-1}}{L}\{W\mathcal{D}_X H + H_c H_\eta + h(1-2\eta U)H\} \;=\; -\frac{q^{-h-1}}{L}HS_q.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same identity, stated in the regular quotient normalisation and with the operators of (4.2) left unexpanded. (i) Lean carries the angular field as swirlProfile = q^{-A-1/2}f = u_theta/r, not as the angular momentum r u_theta = q^{-h}H; Profiles.H = 2Xf and Profiles.E = sqrt(2X) f, so H = sqrt(2X) E and h = A - 1/2 exactly as in (4.1), (4.8). (ii) transport_pullback_add_axialViscosity at e = -A-1/2, alpha = 1, m = 2, source = 0 gives that the inviscid part of transportResidual, namely d_t G + V(d_s G + G/s) + U d_z G with G = swirlProfile, equals q^{-A-3/2}(T_e f + V(f_X + f/X) + U Z_e f); with V = SlowDivergence.radialFlux h 0 U = r u_r (the V_0 of (4.7)) and d_r = r d_s this expression is D_t(r u_theta)/r^2, so the Lean LHS is the paper's LHS divided by r^2 = 2qX. (iii) theta_transport_coefficient equates that bracket to -f S_q / L; dividing the paper's right member by r^2 = 2qX and using H = 2Xf gives -q^{-h-2} f S_q / L, and -A-3/2 = -h-2, so the two agree term for term. (iv) The middle member {W D_X H + H_c H_eta + h(1-2 eta U)H} is literally the negation of the definition StressAlgebra.angularSource (D_X H = x H_x, H_c = D eta + d U with axialExponent h = D = 1/2 - h, coordinateFactor eta = d = 1 - eta^2), and Profiles.angularSource instantiates it at (h, eta, X, W, U, H, H_X, H_eta) with Profiles.W the W of (4.8). (v) The second equality of (4.14) is angular_source_logarithmic_form, which writes the logarithmic slopes as x H_x / H and H_eta / H, where the paper writes l = D_X log H and (log E)_eta; these agree because H = sqrt(2X) E and X, eta are independent, so H_eta / H = (log E)_eta.
